newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish co-op banks seen doubling pre-tax in '96.
newsitem.headline: Polish co-op banks seen doubling pre-tax in '96.

text.p: Poland's cooperative banks grouped in Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) should double their 1995 pre-tax profit to 125.6 million zlotys this year, BGZ's chairman said on Wednesday.

Antoni Magdon told Reuters in an interview that the cooperative banks with large bad debts could meet the required eight-percent solvency ratio if the finance ministry extended them an income tax holiday until the end of 1996.
BGZ groups 1,149 of Poland's more than 1,500 cooperative banks.

Last year the BGZ member banks, which jointly hold 33.5 percent of BGZ, netted 67 million zlotys after the finance ministry granted them income tax relief. The rest of BGZ is held by the state treasury.
Magdon said that if the ministry allowed the cooperative banks to retain all profits this year as well, they would be able to boost their capital to the required level.
He also said that in the first three quarters of 1996 BGZ group banks made a total pre-tax profit of 76 million zlotys, with 1,083 banks showing a profit and 66 losses.
Magdon said a dozen or more of the banks would have to be liquidated while the rest would undergo restructuring under the central bank's supervision.
